scope: Predicting nitrogen removal performance in literature-based anammox processes

matched: 15 input variables (6 categorical, 9 numerical) selected based on pairwise correlation analysis (Fig. S3)
7 output variables predicted separately: effluent NH4+-N, NO3--N, NO2--N, TIN, NH4+-N removal efficiency, TIN removal efficiency, NARR
GBM-like models (GBM and XGBoost) demonstrated advantages across all 7 output variables (Table 1)
GBM characteristics: regularization against overfitting, missing value handling, tree-pruning, parallel processing, imbalanced data handling
Literature evidence of GBM in WWTP applications: influent total nitrogen simulation and energy consumption
High training R2 (0.991-0.999) and low training MAE demonstrated utility of big dataset
Testing performance (R2 = 0.814-0.993) exceeded validation performance due to leaderboard sorting
